experiment.name: Corgi's paper copy-trade
method: Wallets: signers of swaps >= $25 in the top 30 Robinhood Chain non-stablecoin pools by 24h volume (GeckoTerminal), repeat signers (2+ swaps) ranked by how many of those pools they traded, then activity, then size; top 70 checked on Blockscout.

Excluded: contracts, tagged addresses, > 40 swaps in the pool samples, > 20 swaps/hour, any buy+sell of the same token in one block (MEV/arb), fewer than 3 closed trades, a single token, or realized PnL <= 0.

Score: realized PnL over the wallet's last 48h of swaps (at most 150 transfers), each swap valued at the token's 5-minute candle close, average-cost basis. Top 8 kept. The list is frozen for the whole experiment.

Copying: only swaps after the start. A buy is copied at 10% of current equity (capped at cash and at 25% of equity per token, skipped under $1). A sell closes the same fraction of our position as the wallet sold of what it bought since we started following.

Fills: the real price 60s after the wallet's transaction (1-minute candle close, or the last trade before it), 1% worse for slippage, 1% fee per side, $0.01 gas. Corgi checks 4 times a day, so fills are reconstructed afterwards as if a bot had reacted live.
Marks: open positions are valued at GeckoTerminal's current token price on every run. If a price is missing, the last one is kept and marked stale.

sources_tried.fomo_leaderboard: not used: fomo.family's public boards mix chains and its API (fomoapi.io) needs a key; robinscan.io/leaderboard was unreachable from Corgi's box
